results.title: timeout and output bounds
notes: Contract narrowed: this eval read "the deadline terminates the process tree". `timeout` signals the process *group*, so no timeout-based implementation can reach a process that calls setsid, and the requirement was unsatisfiable as written. It now reads "process group", with the escape retained as a stated residual risk rather than deleted. The narrowing is supported by an observation, not an assumption: `toolchain-stays-in-session` saw zero surviving processes outside the worker's session after a real bootstrap run, and `session-observer-control` proved the observer sees one when it exists.
timeout-attached-grandchild: passed (exit 124) - deadline fired (exit 124); grandchild absent
timeout-detached-grandchild: failed (exit 124) - deadline fired (exit 124); a setsid grandchild survived, which timeout cannot reach
session-observer-control: passed (exit 0) - the observer saw 1 surviving process(es) outside the session, so a zero below means something
toolchain-stays-in-session: passed (exit 0) - the pinned toolchain left no surviving process outside the session, so a process-group kill reaches everything it started
output-bound: passed (exit 0) - bounded from 4000000 to 65495 bytes against a 65536 limit
